account:
Something unusually coordinated is happening around this evening's great-hall appointment. The innkeeper identified a hospitality committee consisting of himself, builder and freight. He says its bread is reserved for tonight's gathering and promises to discuss everything at eighteen hundred. I agreed not to arrive early. The secretary will escort me precisely then, but says no agenda or preparatory papers have been supplied. Freight has separately checked that the hall will be available. These arrangements suggest a planned gathering whose purpose is deliberately being kept from me, though I do not yet know why.

Yesterday there was extensive baking; this morning the neighbour reported 201 fresh loaves in the hall, baked yesterday. I have not personally verified that count. A mill-side villager now reports seeing builder carrying a sack of bread at the bakery and at square_north_1. That fits the hospitality preparations. The same villager mentioned a 'bridge or port change' at the bakery, involving baker, freight, innkeeper and neighbour, but gave no clear explanation or time. Another nearby villager used a similar phrase. This is only an unclear report, not proof of any actual infrastructure change.

My best guess is a substantial communal event, perhaps a surprise occasion or announcement, with bread being collected for its guests. A bridge or port matter is another possibility, but the evidence is too vague to connect it confidently. I have no evidence of wrongdoing. The neighbour is curious too, although the villager's report places them among those at the bakery.

Ordinary business continues: I read my appointments this morning and have reached the mill at ten for the grain inspection. Later come lunch at home, council letters at thirteen, tea with the neighbour at fifteen, office at sixteen thirty, and the hall at eighteen. No council letters or accounts have reached the secretary, and the location of the account ledgers remains unresolved. I have asked the secretary to inquire with whoever normally handles them.
